title: How Benzene Swaps an H Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Swap one Lego brick, one relay runner or one bead, and the whole thing still stands. Benzene does the same: it swaps a hydrogen for a new group and keeps its ring. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 9, Hydrocarbons) we learn electrophilic substitution.

On the molecule bench, anhydrous AlCl3 makes Cl+, curved arrows show the pi electrons attacking it, the sigma complex (arenium ion) forms and spreads its charge by resonance, and AlCl4- removes the proton to restore the ring. Then nitration, halogenation, sulphonation and Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation link by link, nitration step by step, and the additions benzene makes only when pushed hard. Then the exam trap, an original JEE/NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 96 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Swap one, keep the whole
0:30 What is electrophilic substitution
1:00 The molecule bench: the three step mechanism
1:52 Substitution vs addition
2:05 Pause and think: the sigma complex
2:20 Five swaps, link by link
3:10 Worked example: nitration step by step
3:46 When benzene adds, and combustion
4:08 Exam trap: the nitration electrophile
4:31 Practice question (JEE/NEET pattern)
5:09 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Directive Influence and Carcinogenicity. Why does a new group choose its seat?
